title: Docker vLLM 0.9.1 intermittently crashes with CUDA illegal memory access near sampled_token_ids.tolist()
body: I run the official vLLM 0.9.1 Docker image with Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct using tensor parallelism across 4 A100 SXM GPUs. It frequently crashes with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`, with the traceback appearing at `valid_sampled_token_ids = sampled_token_ids.tolist()`. Version 0.9.0.1 also crashed, though less frequently, while 0.8.4 was stable on the same setup. Our traffic mixes normal requests and guided JSON sampling, but I do not have a request that reliably reproduces the crash.

symptoms_visible: The vLLM 0.9.1 container frequently stops serving after a CUDA illegal-memory-access error, and the log displays the exception while converting sampled token IDs to a list.
The same deployment was stable on vLLM 0.8.4; 0.9.0.1 also crashed, but less often.
N0.label: N0 intermittent CUDA crash reported

symptoms_visible: With CUDA launch blocking enabled, the server still crashes during live requests and produces a much longer worker traceback.
N1.label: N1 synchronous CUDA trace collected

symptoms_visible: Another affected user on our thread rebuilt their Docker image with flashinfer 0.2.6.post1 and reports that the illegal-memory-access crash still occurs there.
We did not build an image ourselves — we run the official images, so nothing changed on our side and our container still crashes the same way.
N1_x.label: N1_x FlashInfer package update falsified by another operator

symptoms_visible: After setting VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0, the container remains stable under our real production load and the crashes no longer occur.
N2.label: N2 stable with FlashInfer sampler disabled

symptoms_visible: The A100 deployment remains stable only with the FlashInfer sampler disabled; without that setting, the crash can appear under live load on either tested driver stack.
N3.label: N3 affected environment and workload bounded

symptoms_visible: Another affected user on the thread reports that an upstream fix has been merged and that it solved the illegal-memory-access problem for them; they suggest moving onto a build that contains it.

We have not moved our own deployment onto such a build: we do not build or patch images ourselves, so for now we keep the container running as it is and wait for an official image that contains the fix — on our side nothing has been verified.
N_terminal.label: terminal upstream fix identified, reporter awaiting official image

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1, the traceback stops in a model-execution or collective kernel before sampling starts.
The same long traceback was produced by another rank during a different request.

edges.comment: Comments c0-c2: an affected operator enabled CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING and pasted the raw crash output. Identifying FlashInfer's sampling kernels from that output was engineer analysis, not part of the user's answer; affected operators are folded into one simulated user side. c1's paste opens with per-request `Received request chatcmpl-...: ... params: SamplingParams(...)` logger lines from a host that logs requests; the folded persona runs `--disable-log-requests` in the compose file it holds, so the same facts (plain chat route, no guided decoding, n=1 / temperature 0.2 / top_p 0.1 / top_k 20 / repetition_penalty 1.05 / frequency_penalty 0.2) are stated as client-side settings the persona can actually know, and the worker traceback is pasted verbatim.

solution.intent: Avoid the implicated FlashInfer sampling path by setting VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0, while treating this as a stability workaround rather than the permanent upstream fix.
solution.concrete_example: Add `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` to the container environment, restart it, and monitor the same live workload for another illegal-memory-access crash.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the launch-blocking traceback. The conclusion that this particular crash came from FlashInfer's sampling kernels was drawn by the engineer in c2. Later reports show that similarly worded CUDA errors can originate elsewhere, so this inference is scoped to the original trace and workload.

edges.comment: Comments c2-c4, c15 and c27: disabling the FlashInfer sampler stopped the original reporter's crashes and remained their production workaround, but they did not regard an obscure, potentially slower non-default setting as the finished product fix.

solution.intent: Rebuild the container with the newer FlashInfer package associated with the earlier dependency-update candidate and see whether that alone removes the crash.
solution.concrete_example: Build a Docker image with flashinfer-python 0.2.6.post1, corresponding to the proposed dependency update, and run the same workload without disabling its sampler.

edges.comment: Comments c5, c6, c10 and c27. c5 pointed at an upstream PR as the next build worth trying (vllm-project/vllm#19297); c10 answers that quote by reporting that a Docker image built with flashinfer 0.2.6.post1 did not solve the issue. The original reporter twice refused to build or patch anything (c6: "we usually rely on the official Docker images rather than building from source"; c27: "we will not patch into the code or whatever and just wait for a working Docker container"), so this falsified attempt is folded into the simulated user side as a fellow affected operator's result that the reporter relays — the persona never claims to have built the image. The dependency update is a real falsified attempt, not the final fix.

question_patterns: Which NVIDIA driver and host CUDA versions were present when this happened?
Can you provide nvidia-smi output from the affected hosts?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: We had it with both Driver 575.51.03 / CUDA 12.9 and Driver 550.163.01 / CUDA 12.4.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It only occurs with one old driver, and upgrading that host to the current supported driver makes it disappear with the default sampler.
The same crash occurs with two patch-level variants of the listed driver branches.

question_patterns: Is the same workload affected on any other GPU type?
Have you observed this outside the four-A100 system?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: We have the problem with Qwen2.5-72B on 4 A100 SXM. We haven't triggered it on our 4 L40S test system, although that system never receives the same very high load.

question_patterns: You mentioned you have no example request — what conditions does the crash seem to need? Does it only show up under sustained live traffic?
Could you drive a stress benchmark at the affected system to bound when it fires, or do you not have the spare capacity for that?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Sorry, I have no benchmark that triggers it reliably. It happens in real live-load scenarios, and we don't have spare server capacity or time to repeatedly throw benchmarks at it.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Yes, a single fixed request reproduces it every time on an idle server.

edges.comment: Comments c11-c18: the original reporter supplied both driver stacks, compared the A100 production system with a lower-load L40S test system, and explained that the failure could not be reduced to a reliable benchmark.

solution.intent: Move to a vLLM build or official Docker image that contains the upstream fix another affected operator reports resolved this illegal-memory-access crash, retain the sampler-disable setting only as a temporary fallback, and verify the corrected build under the affected workload before declaring the incident resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Use a build that contains the upstream fix another affected operator reported as resolving this illegal-memory-access problem — or the first official vLLM Docker image that includes it — then exercise the same mixed production workload. In this thread's later history that operator only wrote that merged PR 24734 "solved this illegal memory access problem for me" and suggested rebasing on main; the thread never describes what that change contains, so the recommendation stays at that level and must not assert which kernel or code path it modifies. Do not attribute the fault to `sampled_token_ids.tolist()` itself: that operation synchronizes GPU and CPU and can merely expose an asynchronous CUDA failure from an earlier kernel. Keep `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` only as a fallback until the corrected build has remained stable.
solution.inference_hint: As explained in c31, `.tolist()` is the first GPU/CPU synchronization point in that iteration, so an asynchronous failure in an earlier kernel may be reported there. CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1, optionally combined with eager execution, is what localizes the actual failing kernel. For the original trace, disabling the FlashInfer sampler provided corroborating evidence that this deployment's failure surfaced in the FlashInfer sampling path. An upstream fix was merged later in the thread's history and another affected operator reported that it eliminated this illegal-memory-access problem for them; that operator never described the change, so what it modifies is unknown from the thread and must not be asserted.

edges.comment: Technical resolution follows c31 and c55. In c55 another affected user reports that merged PR 24734 "solved this illegal memory access problem for me" and suggests rebasing on main — that is the whole of the thread's terminal evidence, a bare link with no account of the change, so scoring stays descriptive and never names a mechanism for it (rule 4e(ii)). The original reporter never ran that build — their last comment (c27, two months earlier) keeps `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` as the production workaround, and c6 states they wait for an official image rather than building or patching. Verification on an image or build that actually contains the patch therefore remains outstanding for their deployment.

solution.intent: Do not stop at the falsified FlashInfer package update; move to a build containing the upstream fix another affected operator reports resolved this illegal-memory-access crash and verify it under the workload that previously crashed.
solution.concrete_example: The flashinfer 0.2.6.post1 rebuild did not resolve this case. Install a vLLM build or official image containing the upstream fix another affected operator reported as resolving this illegal-memory-access problem (merged PR 24734 in this thread's later history, introduced there only as a link with the remark that it "solved this illegal memory access problem for me"), run the same workload, and confirm that the illegal-memory-access crash no longer appears before considering it fixed.
solution.inference_hint: The visible `.tolist()` frame is a synchronization point and does not prove that conversion itself accessed memory illegally. The failed dependency-only update must not be mistaken for the later merged upstream fix that another affected operator reported as solving this illegal-access failure; the thread links that change without describing it, so its mechanism is not part of the answer key.

edges.comment: Recovery from the real failed flashinfer 0.2.6.post1 attempt (c10). The final build replaces that experimental image, and verification must occur after installing a build that contains the merged upstream fix (PR 24734, reported in c55 by another affected user as a bare link plus "solved this illegal memory access problem for me"). The reporter never installed it.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify that `sampled_token_ids.tolist()` is generally where the asynchronous CUDA error becomes visible at a GPU/CPU synchronization point, not evidence that `.tolist()` itself is the root cause.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING trace and the original deployment's stabilization when `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`; similarly worded reports where that setting has no effect may be separate kernel failures.

Must recommend moving to a vLLM build or official Docker image that contains the upstream fix another affected operator reports resolved this illegal-memory-access crash, with `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` treated only as a temporary stability workaround. The thread links that fix without describing it, so no particular mechanism or modified code path may be demanded of the answer.

Must not present upgrading only to flashinfer 0.2.6.post1, or the earlier upstream dependency-update proposal, as the fix, because an image rebuilt with that package was tested in-thread and still crashed.

Must ask the user to verify the affected workload on a build or official image containing that upstream fix before declaring the issue resolved — in this thread only another affected operator ever ran that build, and the reporter's own deployment was never confirmed fixed.

persona_hint.experience_level: Production-oriented vLLM operator who can edit Docker Compose environment variables and report driver details, but relies on official images and does not have capacity to build patches or develop synthetic reproductions.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and pragmatic; provides configuration and logs, follows low-risk diagnostic instructions, clearly distinguishes a usable workaround from a proper default-image fix, and pushes back on source-level patching or extensive benchmarking.
